subject: killer whale
title: An Orca Washed Up With 7 Sea Otters Inside It, All Swallowed Whole

scenes.text: A dead orca washed up with seven sea otters inside it.
Orcas don't normally eat sea otters. And they almost never swallow prey whole.
Six otters were intact in her stomach. Together, all seven weighed two hundred fifty-eight pounds.
Her DNA said she belonged thousands of miles away, near Alaska. No one from her group had been seen here.
Scientists think she was starving, far from home, and gulped whatever she could catch.
The seventh otter was stuck in her throat. It may be what killed her.

description:
In 2020 a female killer whale stranded on one of Russia's Commander Islands in the Bering Sea. Researchers found six whole sea otters in her stomach and a seventh lodged between her mouth and esophagus; together they weighed 117 kg (258 lb).
DNA showed she was a Bigg's killer whale from the Aleutians-to-California population, the first ever found in the western Pacific. The study, in Aquatic Mammals (2023), suggests she was starving and that the otter in her throat may have killed her.
Why do you think she swam so far from home?
first_comment: Orcas usually tear prey apart and eat only the fattiest parts, which makes seven whole otters even stranger. What do you think drove her that far?
